subject: Agriculture
title: Restaurant and Retail Waste
description: One-minute skill: Restaurant and Retail Waste.

hook.text: An average US restaurant wastes 25,000–75,000 pounds of food per year. Buffets are the worst offenders.

buildup.text: Oversized portions, unpredictable demand, and strict health regulations all contribute to commercial food waste.

discovery.text: Apps like Too Good To Go sell surplus restaurant and bakery food at a discount, reaching 80 million users.

twist.text: Good Samaritan laws protect food donors from liability—yet most businesses don't know these protections exist.

climax.text: France banned supermarkets from throwing away edible food in 2016—requiring donation to food banks instead.

punchline.text: One country's law turned trash into meals. The food was always fine—just unsold.

quiz.question: What did France do about supermarket food waste in 2016?
options: Banned disposal of edible food, requiring donation to food banks
